Experimental Windows utility

iCUE
Memory Guard

A local patch for identified memory allocation paths in iCUE’s CPU identification service and CPUID SDK. Keep verified originals and restore them when needed.

Experimental software.

Modified vendor files lose valid vendor signatures. Instability or loss of sensor functionality is possible, and updates may overwrite the fix. Windows security policies may block the modified files.

See exact hashes and test coverage

Apply once.
Keep recovery close.

Setup creates the modified pair from your installed originals, verifies the results and reloads the affected service. The original files remain available for a guarded restore.

An iCUE update may replace the fix or invalidate patch ownership. Unknown vendor files are preserved. There is no automatic reapplication to an unfamiliar build.

No background
guard to run.

Uses Windows’ built-in PowerShell 5.1. Adds no resident process, service, scheduled task, tray icon or driver. No separate runtime or framework installation is required.

Setup does not require a Windows reboot or a change to certificate trust or system security policy.

Install. Check. Restore.

  1. 01

    Verify and install.

    Verify the download, then run Setup as administrator. Compatibility is checked before the local patch is applied. Sensor readings may pause while the service reloads.

  2. 02

    Check after updates.

    Use the manager’s read-only Status and Check actions after an iCUE update. A newer image can replace the fix. Do not copy older patched files over updated vendor files.

  3. 03

    Restore when needed.

    Use the Restore action or uninstall through Windows Installed apps. Restoration is limited to exact patched files owned by the tool. Keep recovery material if a conflict is reported.

What the local tests show.

An approximately eight-minute heap trace of the patched pair showed stable sampled BSTR counts and no continuing growth stacks. CPU temperature, load reporting and fan response were exercised locally.

These finite results do not prove that every memory leak is fixed or cover every game, sensor or system.

Read validation and limits

Before you install.

Why might Windows warn about the publisher?+

The installer is self-signed with the JZB Apps experimental key. This does not establish public Windows trust or SmartScreen reputation. Use the release’s public certificate, signed checksum manifest and verification scripts to check your download. No certificate is automatically trusted.

Does it support future iCUE updates?+

Compatibility depends on exact tested file contents. A small update can change those contents, even with a familiar version label. Unknown files are preserved. This release does not automatically patch an unfamiliar build.

What if restore or uninstall reports a conflict?+

Keep the recovery material and report the Status/Check result. Uninstall stops if an owned patch cannot be safely restored. If iCUE is absent or a vendor update replaced the files, verified recovery material may be retained; older files are not restored over unknown vendor contents.

Support from JZB Apps

Include the app, Windows and iCUE versions, the manager’s Status/Check result and a description of the problem. Review reports for personal paths before sharing.
